summary: @ornikar/jest-config-react preinstall drops Bun runtime to execute obfuscated payload
details: package.json declares `preinstall: node setup.mjs`. setup.mjs is written in obfuscator.io-style (mangled identifiers `_0x488df8`, `_0x52943e`, wrapped call-site dictionaries around fs/https/child_process/zlib) and, at install time, downloads the Bun runtime archive from `https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13/<arch>.zip`, extracts it to a temp directory, chmods it executable, and invokes the fresh Bun binary against the sibling file `math_init.js`. `math_init.js` is a 727KB `// @bun @bun-cjs` bundle using string-array + character-code decoder obfuscation with `with` statements to defeat strict-mode static parsers; its network destinations and runtime behavior are hidden behind the encoded string table. A Jest React preset has no legitimate need to fetch a second language runtime at preinstall to execute an obfuscated sibling script. The pattern matches the alternate-runtime-dropper shape: an unrelated runtime is fetched specifically so that Node-based install-time scanners do not observe the payload's execution.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
